title: Not breathing — push on the chest
applies_to: An adult or a child over 8 who does not answer you and is not breathing normally.

citations.source: European Resuscitation Council Guidelines 2021: Basic Life Support
American Heart Association Guidelines for CPR and ECC 2020
citations.section: Adult Basic Life Support: compression-only CPR for lay rescuers

citations.source: WHO and IFRC International First Aid, Resuscitation and Education Guidelines 2020

steps.text: Tap their shoulders and shout their name. Ask loudly if they are okay.
If they do not answer, look at their chest for up to 10 seconds. Normal breathing means the chest rises and falls. Slow gasping is not normal breathing.
Call for help now. Put the phone on speaker and set it down so both your hands are free.
Lay them flat on their back on the floor or other hard surface.
Put the heel of one hand in the middle of their chest. Put your other hand on top and lock your fingers together.
Keep your arms straight and press straight down hard, about 5 cm deep. Let the chest come all the way back up after each press.
Press at a steady speed of about 2 presses every second. That is faster than it feels natural, so count out loud to keep the speed up.
Do not stop. Keep pressing until help takes over from you, or the person wakes up and starts breathing normally.
If someone brings a defibrillator, switch it on and do exactly what the machine says out loud. Keep pressing until it tells you to stop.

do_not: Do not stop to look for a pulse. It is hard to feel and looking for it wastes time the heart does not have.
Do not lift your hands off the chest between presses.
Do not stop because you hear or feel a rib move. Keep pressing.
Do not wait to be told you are allowed. If they are not breathing, pressing is the only thing that helps.
escalate_if: They start breathing normally — stop pressing and roll them onto their side.
You are too tired to keep pressing hard — swap with someone else, and take less than 10 seconds to change over.
They are a baby or small child — press with two fingers or one hand, and press less deep.
